chapter: Opinions on playing and old New Orleans
title: No union, subbing and a Tuxedo band job anecdote
summary: Bands were strict, there was no union in the early days, and Foster tells of covering jobs between two bands.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: And we had fun. There was no all. See? And we were more strict. The bands were more strict back in them days. And we didn't have no union. We worked with the white union. And we didn't work under no skills. The college didn't have no union. But if you come to hire me, and we'll cut on that price, you just wish to not, you just wish.

You just wish to hire me. Cause you go to him, he gonna tell you the same thing. Somebody you been hired for, so what's happened? He'll call you, what's the so and so, what's happened? Just like, just like when, when one of the bass players get fired out of the band, and they call me up, I call him, I call him, what's the matter with you? Just like, one or two, he's gonna fire out the band, what's the matter to? You know where he'll want me to play. Well he got to tell me, if he don't, he's gonna tell me, just right. Just like, originally wanna, I was late coming on the job one night and had hired Oak at the Pennsylvania Hall. Pennsylvania Hall. See? Cause me and Oak, we're always like one family down here, see?

So this, this is an uptown band, you know? Tuxedo band, an uptown band. So, see, I had Oak to come in. So when the Oak come in, he said, well man, Oak gonna finish the night. Oak said, no man, not like that.
No, things don't happen like that.
Force to play, or I, you ain't got no bass. You want me to force them both to play, yeah. You know?

But what it is with mine, he used to always be late coming on the job. When I'd go, I'd play with the Tuxedo band, we'd play at like St. Charles Hotel. There'd be two bands, one band over there, one band over there. I'd play this set with my band, and when that band started playing I'd just run over there and play with them. Till the Oak didn't come that night. Man had a pay-off cause I didn't play it for him, see? That's the way we used to wake it. I wouldn't take it, and he couldn't give it to me. Yeah, I've heard of them. They do that. They do that. They do that.

See, but really, them guys from uptown, they was used to waking like we'd wake. And when I started, I said, well, okay man, I'll see you all. Good night. Because me and Johnny had a party at our house, a fish to go in. I'd give them two months notice and he said we was dirty.

Yeah, he said we was dirty. We was going to the giant Charlotte Cref Band, me and Johnny. I was late getting on the job cause I had a little dinner at my house, you know. So Oak stayed all night. Stayed all night there with us anyhow. We used to do them kind of things, man. We've done them very good.
